title: 3-Digit by 2-Digit Multiplication Word Problems
intro: Use partial areas to explain three-digit by two-digit multiplication.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Split both side lengths by place value. Label the smaller rectangles and add every partial area.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

126 × 24 = 126 × (20 + 4)
= 2,520 + 504 = 3,024 square feet

Split 126 into 100 + 20 + 6. Each cell is an area in square feet.
Width100 feet20 feet6 feetRow total
20 feet2,0004001202,520
4 feet4008024504

All six smaller areas belong in the total. Multiplying only the hundreds by the tens, or forgetting one row, leaves part of the field uncounted.

Ask your student

Which section of the rectangle does this product represent?

If your student needs help

If a partial product is missing, check each row and column of the area model.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet contains four original rectangle-area stories with lengths from 100 to 999 feet and widths from 10 to 99 feet. Zero digits and multiples of ten can occur, but a set does not guarantee a particular digit pattern. Use the working space for the two partial products, regrouping marks, and their sum. The key supplies the equation and final area; the child still explains the calculation.
